To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the numbers to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6{x}^{2} & >-3x \\ -6{x}^{2}+3x & >0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y=-6{x}^{2}+3x$ lies above the $x$-axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ -3x(2x-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=0$ and $x=\frac{1}{2},$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14029391/assets/3dff64c74abd4981c69686cbbf7d79fdd49c7a7fde3bb266b2b6e11c441bcf20.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
-6{x}^{2}+3x>0,
$$

we look for the part of the parabola that is above the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $0<x<\frac{1}{2}.$
